notes: The session's WebSearch allowance ran out after eight searches of this slice (the first two candidates); everyone after that was researched by reading pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: government sites, party sites, local newspapers' own search pages, Wikipedia's API. Checked afterwards against the campaign website cell of the Secretary of State's list, read by the kit's own step on a scratch copy of the database (python -m ballot.local_sites files --db <copy>): the eight websites below are the eight this slice's candidates filed, and nobody else in the slice filed one. A candidate with a site they did not file could still have been missed.

Jennifer Geisler's campaign site shows, under "Supported by", the logos of the Senate District 35 DFL and the Anoka County DFL beside the DFL Senior Caucus's. Only the Senior Caucus publishes its endorsement on a page of its own that could be read (the address the state party gives for Senate District 35's site no longer answers, and it gives none for the county unit), so only that one is recorded.

The Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (mncourts.gov) answers both the kit's reader and WebFetch with 403, so the two judges have no official page here and their appointments rest on newspaper reports. The Yellow Medicine County and Houston County sites could not be read either (robots.txt asks scripts to stay out; the other fails its secure handshake).
Ages printed in ABC Newspapers' voter guides (Jennifer Geisler 64 in July 2026; Tammy Gimpl 53 in October 2024) are not birth years and were left out.

For whoever holds race 2026-MN-1010-17486 (East Bethel council): ABC Newspapers reported on August 7, 2026 that Tim Miller, who is on the November list, died on August 1 after filing, and that his name stays on the ballot: https://www.hometownsource.com/abc_newspapers/community/east-bethel-council-member-tim-miller-dies-at-60/article_80983ad4-2711-4e0a-b53b-5e3f67762138.html

verifier_notes: Every address in the file was re-opened on 2026-10-02 with the kit's reader. Three school district pages (North Branch, Hermantown, Fairmont) keep their words in the page's embedded data rather than its visible markup; the names and titles were read there.

The Minnesota DFL's endorsed list carries no year in its text; it was taken as the 2026 list because it names Senate candidates (the Senate is on the ballot in 2026 and was not in 2024) and its pictures were uploaded in 2026.
Samakab Hussein's quoted sentence stands on his own site beside a message dated November 2024; the site does not say which year's endorsement it means.
The Legislative Reference Library's page for Leon M. Lillie also carries ancestry and religion; neither is recorded here.
